The title "Disruption of threat actors" is prominently displayed at the top, followed by a detailed description of the actions taken against five state-affiliated malicious actors and their associated OpenAI accounts.
    
    The text explains that these actors were terminated due to their misuse of OpenAI services for various malicious activities, including:
    
    * Charcoal Typhoon: researching companies and cybersecurity tools, debugging code, and generating scripts for phishing campaigns
    * Salmon Typhoon: translating technical papers, retrieving publicly available information on intelligence agencies and regional threat actors, assisting with coding, and researching ways to hide processes on a system
    * Crimson Sandstorm: scripting support for app and web development, generating content for spear-phishing campaigns, and researching ways malware could evade detection
    * Emerald Sleet: identifying experts and organizations focused on defense issues in the Asia-Pacific region, understanding publicly available vulnerabilities, helping with basic scripting tasks, and drafting content for phishing campaigns
    * Forest Blizzard: using OpenAI services primarily for open-source research into satellite communication protocols and radar imaging technology, as well as for support with scripting tasks
    
    The text also mentions that additional technical details on the nature of the threat actors and their activities can be found in a Microsoft blog post published on the same day.
    
    Overall, the image provides a clear and concise overview of the actions taken against these malicious actors and the measures being taken to prevent their future activities.

1769824039986446766 [2024-03-18] @GarrisonLovely 💜 13 🔁 1
Sam Altman just did probably his longest interview since his ouster. He talks about the board drama, Ilya, GPT-5, and his top worries regarding AGI [1]. Lex’s questions are softballs ofc, but there’s still a good amount of newsworthy bits (I’ve added relevant context) 🧵 https://t.co/nY5TWHjM7T
Images:
  - [Image #0] [PIC NOT AVAILABLE]

===

1769824047334875184 [2024-03-18] @GarrisonLovely 💜 1
Sam says he saw Ilya playing with a puppy at a dinner party recently (though it’s left unsaid if that party happened before or after the ouster).
↓
1769824048735731791 [2024-03-18] @GarrisonLovely 💜 1
Sam claims that Larry Summers was suggested by the old board during the drama and that Sam had suggested Bret Taylor prior to the ouster. (Musk’s lawsuit claims that Taylor and Summers were hand-picked by Altman, but didn’t provide evidence to support this [3].)
↓
1769824050216374652 [2024-03-18] @GarrisonLovely 💜 2
Sam says he’s grateful that Adam D’Angelo stayed on the board (D’Angelo is the one remaining board member who voted to fire Sam).
↓
1769824051822809266 [2024-03-18] @GarrisonLovely 
Sam says he initially accepted the board’s decision and was excited to work closely with researchers again, but that OpenAI’s exec team suggested that he come back. (Reporting and the employee letter indicate that the exec team wanted him back, but I’m not sure if there’s been any reporting either way on whether Sam was pulled back in or proactively wanted to be reinstated.)
↓
1769824053399814398 [2024-03-18] @GarrisonLovely 💜 1
Of the board drama: “it felt very painful, but I felt a lot of love that whole weekend it was not — other than that one moment Sunday night [when the board announced Emmett Shear as interim CEO] — I would not characterize my emotions as anger or hate.”
↓
1769824054825886064 [2024-03-18] @GarrisonLovely 💜 5
RE the Musk lawsuit, Sam says he would pick a different name if he were starting over. He says that the “Open” in OpenAI means putting stuff in people’s hands for free, pointing to the lack of ads and other efforts to monetize the free version of ChatGPT. (This echoes Ilya’s 2016 email to Musk about what openness means once they stop open sourcing everything [4]).
↓
1769824056302350490 [2024-03-18] @GarrisonLovely 
Sam says that if he were an artist, he would like to be able to opt out of AI making art in his style and/or get compensated when AI generates art in his style.
↓
1769824057749320111 [2024-03-18] @GarrisonLovely 💜 2
“I think [gpt-4] kinda sucks.” and that he expects the delta between 5 and 4 will be similar to the one between 4 and 3.
↓
1769824059166962095 [2024-03-18] @GarrisonLovely 💜 1
RE Q*, Sam says that OpenAI is not good at keeping secrets and has been plagued by a lot of leaks. (Subsequent reporting found that there was no secret letter about Q* shared with the board [5]. To my knowledge, Sam has never pointed that fact out, and his public comments have insinuated that the leak was real.)
↓
1769824060580470837 [2024-03-18] @GarrisonLovely 💜 1
Sam says that OpenAI will release “an amazing model this year,” but is not sure what they’ll call it.
↓
1769824062031667367 [2024-03-18] @GarrisonLovely 💜 1 [(SEED) type=semantic_search]
RE state actors trying to infiltrate OpenAI, “They’re trying!”
↓
1769824063499690137 [2024-03-18] @GarrisonLovely 💜 1
Lex asks if he trusts himself with the power to control AGI. After a long pause, Sam says, “It is important that I nor any other one person have total control over OpenAI or AGI, and I think you want a robust governance system." (He clearly intended to say that it’s important that no one person, himself included, have total control, but it’s a funny place to misspeak.)
↓
1769824064850317631 [2024-03-18] @GarrisonLovely 
Sam says he continues to not want super-voting control in OpenAI. (The Musk lawsuit included an email from Sam reading, “At some point we'd get someone to run the team, but he/she probably shouldn't be on the governance board.” [6]).
↓
1769824066712588732 [2024-03-18] @GarrisonLovely 💜 4 🔁 1
“I continue to think that no company should be making these decisions and that we really need governments to put rules of the road in place.” (Sam has rhetorically supported regulation of AI throughout OpenAI’s history. In an email from the Musk suit Sam wrote “Obviously we’d comply with/aggressively support all regulation.” [7] However, shortly before he was fired, Sam said at a business conference “current models are fine. We don’t need heavy regulation here. Probably not even for the next couple of generations.” [8])
↓
1769824068046315866 [2024-03-18] @GarrisonLovely 💜 5
Sam reiterates his belief that the safest approach to AGI is to have short timelines with a long take off. (I’ve written about how his $7 trillion chip ambitions undercuts this strategy [9].) 
https://t.co/gikIqqgxtF
↓
1769824069686317176 [2024-03-18] @GarrisonLovely 💜 4 🔁 1
He says that loss of control of AGI is not his top worry. (There’s a big split in the AI safety community between being more worried about misuse risk vs. loss of control. If you think that you can get an AGI to be compliant, i.e. the technical alignment problem is solvable, you’ll probably care way more about who develops it first, whether that’s OpenAI or Anthropic, or the US or China. If you think that it’s really hard to get an AGI to do what you want, you’ll tend to favor slowing or stopping the whole race and care far less about who gets it first. People I’ve spoken with at OpenAI tend to worry far more about misuse, whereas people like @ESYudkowsky worry almost entirely about loss of control.)
↓
1769824071250837871 [2024-03-18] @GarrisonLovely 💜 2
Sam critiqued a lot of AI safety folks for focusing so much on the “AI box” problem, i.e. how you keep a superintelligence from escaping containment, without making much progress. He argues that this pushed aside a lot of the other risks. (A lot of the AI box conversation presumed that researchers would be extremely wary of connecting a powerful system to the internet, but have been surprised and exasperated at how eager labs have been to connect their models to the internet and increase their ability to influence the world.)
↓
1769824072672620623 [2024-03-18] @GarrisonLovely 💜 1
I’m often frustrated by how friendly interviews like this are, but they also tend to go longer and get important people to open up more about high-stakes things.

Also, if you enjoyed this, consider subscribing to my Substack:

https://t.co/XXNoZ0EToD
